title: Philly's Biggest Stars Are Throwing a Free July 4th Party — and You're Invited!
summary: Have you ever dreamed of seeing your favorite singers all in one place — for free? This July 4th, that dream comes true in Philadelphia! The city is throwing a huge concert called "One Philly: Unity Concert for America" to celebrate America's 250th birthday. And the lineup is stacked with stars who grew up right in Pennsylvania. Christina Aguilera, Will Smith and DJ Jazzy Jeff, the Roots, Jill Scott, and more will take the stage. Even comedian Wanda Sykes, who lives nearby, will host the six-hour show. The party happens on Benjamin Franklin Parkway, just steps from the famous Liberty Bell. Gates open at 3 p.m., music starts at 5 p.m., and a fireworks show will explode above the Philadelphia Museum of Art at 11:45 p.m. to end the night with a bang. The best part? It's totally free and open to everyone. Organizers hope it will be the biggest free concert in the whole country. Mayor Cherelle L. Parker says it's a "historic homecoming" for the city's brightest stars. So grab your family, pack a picnic, and get ready to sing along. America's birthday party is going to be epic!
why_it_matters: This huge free party lets kids like you feel the excitement of live music and national pride right in the city where America was born.

background_read: America is turning 250 years old in 2026. The Declaration of Independence was signed in Philadelphia in 1776, so the city is a very important part of U.S. history.
Christina Aguilera (a famous pop singer known worldwide) and Will Smith (a movie star and rapper who grew up in West Philadelphia) both come from Pennsylvania and are coming back to perform.
The Liberty Bell is an old cracked bell that became a symbol of freedom, and right next to it is Benjamin Franklin Parkway, a wide avenue where big city celebrations often happen.
Article_Structure: WHO: The city of Philadelphia, Mayor Cherelle L. Parker, and famous Pennsylvania-born artists like Christina Aguilera, Will Smith, and the Roots.
WHAT: A free six-hour concert called "One Philly: Unity Concert for America" ending with a huge fireworks display.
WHERE: Benjamin Franklin Parkway, just steps from the Liberty Bell and the Philadelphia Museum of Art.
WHY: To celebrate America's 250th birthday and give the community a historic, happy gathering.

perspectives.description: Supporters say the concert unites people from all backgrounds, shows off Philadelphia's talent, and gives families a free, unforgettable experience.
Some locals worry about huge crowds, hot weather, and noise in the neighborhoods around the Parkway during the long event.
Historians and city planners note that big public celebrations on Independence Day have been a tradition in Philadelphia for centuries.
